findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the binding-store commit path (reconcile.py post-apply block and reconcile_helpers._commit_binding_store_snapshot) as an edit target and specify how .bridge_state/impossible_links.json is committed to the tickets branch so it survives a concurrent `git merge origin/tickets` between passes.
evidence: reconcile_helpers.py:207-211 stages a fixed list `_rel_files = [git_adapter.BINDINGS_FILE, git_adapter.BINDINGS_RETIRED_FILE, git_adapter.GET_ROTATION_FILE]` — impossible_links.json is not in it
reconcile.py:575-598 docstring: without committing the file to the tickets branch, 'a concurrent git merge origin/tickets ... can clobber the working-tree ... version' between passes
Plan step 1 places the file under .bridge_state/ but the Approach and 'hygiene' section never name the commit/persistence path as an edit target

The plan's stated goal is a 'durable, self-healing memory' that survives passes; AC requires 'The record survives a process restart' — an uncommitted .bridge_state file defeats both if a merge intervenes
findings.finding: The new durable state file .bridge_state/impossible_links.json is not committed to the tickets orphan branch: reconcile_helpers._commit_binding_store_snapshot stages only BINDINGS_FILE, BINDINGS_RETIRED_FILE and GET_ROTATION_FILE, and this commit path (a consumer the change requires updating) is not enumerated in the plan.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (JSON store at .tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/impossible_links.json) and step 3 (durability); AC 'The record survives a process restart'
scenarios: Two overlapping/consecutive Reconcile Bridge passes where a concurrent GHA commit-back merges origin/tickets: the working-tree impossible_links.json is overwritten/lost and every doomed link is re-attempted — the bridge fails to converge exactly as before
findings.suggested_fix: Add impossible_links.json to the staged-file list in _commit_binding_store_snapshot (alongside BINDINGS_FILE/BINDINGS_RETIRED_FILE/GET_ROTATION_FILE), introducing a git_adapter constant for its relative path, and note the reconcile.py post-apply persistence block as touched.

findings.checklist_item: State that deciding_digest for closed_source/redundant_ancestry must cover the RESOLVED (post-hierarchy-redirect) endpoints add_dependency actually validates, not only the caller-supplied source/target, so a status/parent change on a promoted ancestor invalidates the record.
evidence: _links.py:182-227 resolve_hierarchy_link + was_redirected reassigns source_id/target_id to resolved_source/resolved_target BEFORE the cycle (229), level-cycle (244), and closed-source (259) checks
Plan: 'closed_source / redundant_ancestry are decided entirely by the two endpoints, so those digests cover each endpoint's status, parent chain and dep set'
The validator reads resolved endpoints, not the passed source/target; a promotion to an ancestor means the deciding status is the ancestor's
findings.finding: The digest/store keys on the caller-supplied source|target|relation, but add_dependency resolves hierarchy and REDIRECTS endpoints (promotes to a type-tier ancestor) BEFORE running the closed-source, redundant, and cycle validators — so the actual deciding inputs belong to the resolved endpoints, which may differ from the triple the applier passes. The plan does not acknowledge this, risking a digest that omits the redirect target's status/parent and thus fails to invalidate when the true deciding ticket changes.
findings.location: Approach step 1, deciding_digest bullet ('decided entirely by the two endpoints')
scenarios: A redundant/closed verdict fires on a promoted ancestor endpoint; that ancestor is later reopened/reparented but the two original endpoints stay byte-identical, so an endpoint-only digest never invalidates and the now-legitimate link is suppressed indefinitely — the same under-invalidation trap the plan flags only for cycles
findings.suggested_fix: Have deciding_digest resolve the hierarchy the same way add_dependency does (or fold the full parent chain of both endpoints, which already reaches the redirect target) and document that the digest is computed over resolved endpoints; if resolution is uncomputable, fall through to fail-open (attempt the write).

evidence: 6 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the global structural projection feeding cycle digests is computed once per pass and reused, not recomputed per impossible-link record.
evidence: 'A cycle record therefore keys on the global structural projection (every ticket's status/parent/deps)'
No statement that the projection/digest input is memoized per pass
findings.finding: The cycle-record digest keys on a 'global structural projection (every ticket's status/parent/deps)'. The plan does not state whether this projection is computed once per pass and reused across records, or recomputed per impossible-link record, leaving an O(records x N tickets) cost path unspecified.
scenarios: A pass with many recorded cycle impossible-links recomputes the whole-graph projection once per record check
findings.suggested_fix: Note in step 1 that the global projection is snapshotted once per pass and the cycle digest reuses that snapshot.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether Reconcile Bridge passes are serialized; if they can overlap, acknowledge that last-write-wins may drop a just-recorded record (self-heals next pass) rather than implying atomic replace prevents all interleaving.
evidence: 'two overlapping passes cannot interleave a half-written file' addresses torn writes only
Passes 're-dispatch every ~5-6 min' — the plan does not establish passes are strictly serialized, and the store is read-modify-written (read existing, add/prune, write whole file)
findings.finding: The concurrency claim is narrower than the shared-state atomicity check requires: atomic temp-file + os.replace prevents a half-written file (torn write) but does NOT prevent a lost-update race — two overlapping passes each read-modify-write the store, and the later os.replace clobbers a record the other pass just recorded.
scenarios: Two Reconcile Bridge passes overlap; pass A records a new impossible link, pass B (which read the store before A wrote) replaces the file and drops A's record
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note that passes are serialized (single-flight) OR that the read-modify-write is intentionally last-write-wins and self-healing, so a clobbered record is re-recorded next pass.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the impossible-links store design (separate-file rationale, cycle global-projection digest, over-invalidation-preferred asymmetry) in an ADR or AGENTS.md/design-doc update.

No mention of recording the decision (why a separate file from bindings.json, the over-invalidation-preferred rationale) in a durable design doc
findings.finding: The plan documents a novel durable-state pattern (a versioned JSON store with digest-based invalidation semantics and an under/over-invalidation asymmetry rule) but does not capture this architectural decision in any ADR / AGENTS.md / design-doc update.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (new module impossible_links.py) / Deliberately out of scope
scenarios: A future maintainer touching the reconciler or the epic despotic-floriated-leopard REMOVE branch needs to understand why the ADD-branch state file exists and how its digest invalidation works
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC or approach note pointing to a short ADR/AGENTS.md entry documenting the store schema, invalidation keying, and the deliberate asymmetry.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the new impossible_links.py store against the existing alert_store.py (atomic writes, fcntl locking, fail-open reads, cross-pass dedup): either reuse/extend it, or state explicitly that its time-window invalidation cannot express the required structural-digest self-healing invalidation and that a separate store is therefore necessary.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/alert_store.py: append() uses fcntl.LOCK_EX; _atomic_write() uses tempfile+fsync+os.replace; is_deduped(key, repo_root, window_ns) dedups across passes with per-line/per-file fail-open

tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_check_dual_identity_complete.py:131 'Repeated reconciler passes each hit the [same failure]' — alert_store.is_deduped is the existing cross-pass suppression seam
Plan quote: 'A JSON store at .../impossible_links.json ... A separate file from bindings.json on purpose' — justifies separateness only vs bindings.json, never vs alert_store
Differentiator not spelled out: alert_store dedup is window-based (window_ns), the plan needs digest-invalidation self-healing
findings.finding: The plan proposes a new durable JSON store (impossible_links.py) that re-implements durable-store mechanics the codebase already ships in alert_store.py — atomic temp-file+os.replace writes, fcntl-serialized access, per-line/per-file fail-open reads, and cross-pass dedup keyed on a stable key — without acknowledging or comparing against it. alert_store is already the reconciler's canonical mechanism for 'repeated passes hit the same failure, suppress the repeat' (documented in test_check_dual_identity_complete.py). The plausible reason a new store is warranted is that alert_store invalidates on a TIME WINDOW (is_deduped(key, window_ns)) whereas this feature needs STRUCTURAL-DIGEST invalidation (re-attempt when the deciding inputs change) — but the plan never makes that comparison, so the reader cannot tell whether the new module is necessary or a duplicate.
findings.location: Approach §1 (New module impossible_links.py) and §3 (Fail-open and hygiene)
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer sees two overlapping durable cross-pass stores and cannot tell why alert_store was not reused/extended
The new module reimplements atomic-write/fail-open logic that alert_store already tests, risking divergence in the hardening details
